title: Avgolemono
description:
Avgolemono, or Greek chicken and rice soup, gets its name from the egg-lemon mixture that thickens and flavors
it. Our version contains tender shreds of chicken that are poached to perfection by sitting off the heat in hot
broth. We flavored the broth with citrusy coriander and lemon zest that gave it savory depth and enhanced the
soup’s lemon flavor. Processing eggs, yolks, and a portion of the cooked rice in a blender and then stirring this
puree into the hot broth gave our avgolemono a velvety consistency.
If you have homemade chicken broth such as our Classic Chicken Broth, we recommend using it in this recipe, as
it gives the soup the best flavor and body. Our preferred commercial chicken broth is Swanson Chicken Stock.
Use a vegetable peeler to remove strips of zest from the lemons.
ingredients: 1 ½ pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, trimmed
12 (3-inch) strips lemon zest plus 6 tablespoons juice, plus
2 sprigs fresh dill, plus 2 teaspoons chopped
directions: Cut each chicken breast in half (or thirds, depending on the size), lengthwise. Toss with 1 3/4 teaspoons
salt and let stand at room temperature for at least 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes. Cut 8-inch square of
triple-thickness cheesecloth. Place lemon zest, dill sprigs, coriander seeds, peppercorns, and garlic in
center of cheesecloth and tie into bundle with kitchen twine.
Bring broth, rice, and spice bundle to boil in large saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to low, cover, and
cook for 7 minutes. Turn off heat, add chicken, cover, and let stand for 15 minutes.
Transfer chicken to large plate and discard spice bundle. Using two forks, shred chicken into bite-size
Strain the rice (saving the broth), then transfer the rice to blender or food processor (leave any liquid in
pot). Add lemon juice and eggs and yolks to blender and process until smooth, about 1 minute.
Return soup broth to simmer over high heat. Remove pot from heat and stir or whisk in rice/lemon/egg
mixture until fully incorporated. Return chicken and any accumulated juices to pot, heating a little if
